content.user_title: Generate OpenAPI Docs from API Routes
content.value_statement: Manual API docs get stale when routes change. This skill reads route files and builds OpenAPI or Swagger specs for common REST frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Finds route definitions in Express, FastAPI, Flask, NestJS, and Rails projects.
Extracts HTTP methods, paths, parameters, responses, authentication notes, and descriptions.
Creates or updates OpenAPI 3.0 YAML or Swagger documentation files.
Builds JSON Schema request and response definitions from available models and validators.
Adds error responses, security schemes, endpoint tags, and examples when detected.
Suggests an output location and asks for clarification when the location is unclear.
limitations: Requires readable source files; it cannot document endpoints hidden outside available project files.
Generated schemas depend on available models, validators, comments, and tests.
It may need user confirmation for output location or API version.
It does not validate live server behavior or guarantee runtime accuracy.

use_cases.title: Document a Backend Service
use_cases.description: Generate a first OpenAPI spec from existing route files and framework conventions.

use_cases.title: Refresh Public API Docs
use_cases.description: Update existing Swagger documentation after endpoints, schemas, or authentication rules change.

use_cases.title: Audit Endpoint Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare documented endpoints with route files before a release or platform review.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project without API documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scan the route files in this project and create an OpenAPI 3.0 file in the project root.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintain an existing OpenAPI or Swagger file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to update the existing OpenAPI or Swagger file. Preserve custom descriptions and add missing endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Add Schemas and Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve documentation quality using project source context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect validators, DTOs, models, tests, and route comments. Add request schemas, response schemas, and standard error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Framework API
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across mixed framework services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare Express, FastAPI, Flask, NestJS, or Rails routes with current API docs. Report gaps before writing changes.

output_examples.input: Generate docs for the Express user routes.
output_examples.output: Creates an OpenAPI file with Users endpoints, path parameters, request body details, success responses, and error responses.

output_examples.input: Refresh docs for a FastAPI service with Pydantic models.
output_examples.output: Updates endpoint descriptions and connects request and response schemas to detected models.

output_examples.input: Check NestJS controllers against the Swagger file.
output_examples.output: Reports missing controller methods, authentication requirements, and response descriptions before applying updates.

best_practices: Review generated schemas against source models before publishing.
Keep route comments, validators, and tests current so extracted docs stay accurate.
Store the generated OpenAPI file in a predictable docs or project root location.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated docs without checking authentication, error responses, and examples.
Do not overwrite hand-written descriptions without reviewing the diff.
Do not use placeholder server URLs in production documentation.

faq.question: Which frameworks can this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Express, FastAPI, Flask, NestJS, Rails, and similar REST frameworks.

faq.question: Can it update existing OpenAPI files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update OpenAPI or Swagger files and preserve useful existing descriptions when requested.

faq.question: Does it call my API endpoints?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes local source files and documentation patterns. It does not start servers or call endpoints.

faq.question: What output files can it create?
faq.answer: It can create or update files such as openapi.yaml, swagger.json, or documentation files in a docs directory.

faq.question: How accurate are generated schemas?
faq.answer: Accuracy depends on route code, models, validators, comments, and tests available in the project.

faq.question: Can it document authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add Bearer, API key, or OAuth security schemes when the project context supports them.
